title: Where it grows
subtitle: Italy, Alsace and beyond
objectives: Explain how climate and yield shape it

steps.title: A wide map
steps.body: Italy is the largest producer, mostly in the north-east: Veneto, Friuli and Alto Adige. Alsace makes its richest versions. Germany calls it Grauburgunder, for dry styles, or Ruländer, for sweeter ones. Oregon, New Zealand, Australia and Hungary, where it's Szürkebarát, grow it too.

steps.title: Yield and picking
steps.body: The style depends heavily on yield and picking time. High yields and early picking give light, neutral, crisp wine. Low yields and later picking give concentrated, rich, spicy wines with more alcohol. The grape itself is the same; the grower's choices make the difference.

steps.prompt: Match each name to its country.

steps.title: Delle Venezie
steps.body: In Italy, the Delle Venezie DOC, created in 2017, covers Pinot Grigio from Veneto, Friuli and Trentino, the world's largest Pinot Grigio appellation. It aimed to raise quality and control the huge volume produced for export. Alto Adige and Collio make more serious examples.

steps.prompt: What gives a richer, spicier Pinot Gris?
steps.explanation: High yields and early picking give the light, neutral style.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Italy makes the most; Alsace the richest
Yield and picking time decide the style
Delle Venezie DOC covers Italy's huge Pinot Grigio output
